title: Unit comparison from an invertible affine closed-site counit
statement: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $V$ an affine small pro-etale object [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site]. Put $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ [def-pc-scheme], $I=\ker(A\to\Gamma(V\times_XZ,\mathcal O))$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $B$ be the identity object of the affine ind-etale basis over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Suppose evaluation at $B$ takes epimorphisms of set sheaves to surjections. For any adjunction between the canonical closed-site lift and base change [def-exc-closed-site-lift], an invertible counit at $B$ implies that the actual inverse-image adjunction unit on sections at $V$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is a natural isomorphism of abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. No specialization hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09BL (1),(2); Tag 09AC, affine reduction and unit identification

proof.text: Localize at V and use the quotient of its global-sections map by its actual kernel. The inverse-image comparison is the mate of the base-change comparison, so preserves units. The presheaf colimit description and local representatives for sheafification verify the same identification explicitly. If the evaluation comparison uses a different adjunction on the same fixed functors, uniqueness of left adjoints changes the counit by an automorphism; its invertibility is unchanged.

Lift a finite cover of r(B) along v. The left adjoint preserves its finite coproduct, including the empty coproduct; the functor-properties theorem preserves the cover. Identify v(r(B)) with B by the assumed counit, split the resulting cover using projective evaluation and subcanonical Yoneda, then apply r and the invertible unit. This splits the original disjoint-union cover. Local lifts of any epimorphism glue over this union and pull back to r(B), proving weak contractibility there.

Affine closed inverse-image evaluation identifies the inverse-image sections with sheafification of evaluation along v and makes its sheafification unit bijective at r(B). Under adjunction, the original representative (B,id) corresponds to the counit v(r(B))->B. Hence the actual unit is restriction along the invertible counit followed by this bijection. Forgetting abelian groups commutes with the filtered inverse-image colimit and sheafification, so the identified maps are additive; naturality assembles the pointwise isomorphisms. No geometry proving invertibility of the counit is used here.

lean.statement:
theorem isIso_proEtaleUnit_sections_of_closedSiteCounit
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (V : X.ProEt) [IsAffine V.left]
 :
    let A := Γ(V.left, ⊤)
    let I := RingHom.ker (pullback.fst V.hom i).appTop.hom
    let B := AffineProEt.ofEtale (𝟙 (Spec A))
    (∀ (P Q : Sheaf (AffineProEt.topology (Spec A)) (Type (u + 1))) (φ : P ⟶ Q),
      Epi φ → Function.Surjective (φ.hom.app (op B))) →
    ∀ adj : AffineProEt.closedSiteLift A I ⊣ AffineProEt.closedSiteBaseChange A I,
      IsIso (adj.counit.app B) →
      IsIso (Functor.whiskerRight (proEtaleSheafAdjunction i AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).unit
        ((sheafSections (ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj (op V)))
